name: Silicon
occurrence: Second most abundant element in Earth's crust after oxygen, almost entirely as silicate minerals and silica (sand).
notableCharacteristics: Its four-bond tetrahedral bonding pattern mirrors carbon's, which is why silicon-based semiconductor technology underlies essentially every modern computer chip.
whyHere: Sitting directly below carbon with the same four valence electrons, silicon forms similar tetrahedral covalent networks — but its larger atomic size makes those bonds weaker and its conductivity intermediate, which is exactly the metalloid behaviour semiconductors rely on.
didYouKnow: 'Silicon Valley' is named for this element specifically because of the silicon-based semiconductor chips manufactured there starting in the 1970s.
genZNote: Carbon's quieter sibling that ended up running every computer on Earth instead. Understated but everywhere.
